A previously healthy 12-year-old male was referred to the emergency department

attribution_limitations: Table 1 prints the caption "days following paraquat ingestion" for Day 1 to Day 9, but the case text says the patient was referred 7 days after ingestion, gives high serum urea 212 mg/dL and creatinine 8.6 mg/dL on the day of admission, and a discharge BUN 19 mg/dL and Cr 1.3 mg/dL after 9 days. Table 1 Day 1 prints BUN 212 and Day 9 prints BUN 19 and Cr 1,3, so the numbers match in places but the source never says Day 1 is the admission day or Day 9 the discharge day.

Creatinine is 8.6 mg/dL on the day of admission in the text, whereas Table 1 Day 1 (days following paraquat ingestion) prints 10.5 beside a BUN of 212 that equals the text serum urea. The source does not say Day 1 is the day of admission, so the two values are recorded as separate time points with their own literal times.

Table 1 prints no units. WBC, HGB, PLT, ESR, ALT, AST, NA and K cells carry none, and the Cr and BUN cells do not carry the mg/dL used in the text. Many cells use a decimal comma (for example 11,8 and 3,4), which the deterministic measurement parser leaves unparsed, so those cells are kept as printed text with no numeric value.
The Table 1 footnote expands ALT, AST, CR, BUN, WBC, HGB, PLT and ESR but not the NA and K column headers.
Table 1 Day 5 prints BUN as 3,4 between 63 on Day 4 and 34 on Day 6, which is out of line with the serial values and may be a print artefact.

Two blood pressures are stated: 100/75 mm Hg in the On-examination sentence and 90/60 mm Hg in the On-arrival sentence. The Overall-vital-signs sentence then prints 90/60 mm Hg, pulse 71 beats/min and respiratory rate 18 breaths/min without a time and calls the vital signs normal.

The source says dialysis was started "day 3", after "three cessation of dialysis" urea and creatinine reduced to normal, and kidney functions recovered "after 3 cessation dialysis"; the wording is unclear.

The case text says the patient was referred to the emergency department 7 days after ingestion and, in a later sentence, that he followed his parents to a public health city center and then was referred "to this center". The source does not say that "this center" is the named hospital or that the two referral statements describe one referral.

The treatment sentence after admission is ungrammatical: the Ventolin nebulizer and becotide spray have no verb, the antibiotics are "received" during admission, and pantoprazole is added with "and also".

The Discussion says the patient was successfully treated using multi-target comprehensive therapy, while the Introduction names a comprehensive treatment strategy (the Qilu scheme) from the authors' previous work; no sentence says the patient received that scheme or lists what the therapy contained.

The diagnosis sentence cites computed tomography manifestations, and a later sentence says the dynamic changes in the lung CT-scans are shown in Figure 3, but no CT findings, dates or body sites are given in the text.

The source text calls the initial chest x-ray normal (Figure 2). The figure captions in source.json hold only the labels Figure 1 to Figure 3; the original JATS (raw.xml) carries a short statement per figure that was not captured as a segment, and the Figure 2 statement there describes mild bilateral patchy consolidation, which differs from normal. It cannot be cited as evidence.
